'''Kai A. Behrend''' is a German mathematician.  He is a professor at the [[University of British Columbia]] in [[Vancouver, British Columbia]], Canada.

His work is in [[algebraic geometry]] and he has made important contributions in the theory of [[algebraic stack]]s, [[Gromov–Witten invariant]]s and [[Donaldson–Thomas theory]] (cf. [[Behrend function]]). He is also known for [[Behrend's formula]], the generalization of the [[Grothendieck–Lefschetz trace formula]] to algebraic stacks.

He is the recipient of the 2001 [[Coxeter–James Prize]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cms.math.ca/awards/coxeter-james-prize/|title=Coxeter-James Prize|accessdate=17 December 2021}}</ref> the 2011 [[Jeffery–Williams Prize]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cms.math.ca/awards/jeffery-williams-prize/|title=Jeffery-Williams Prize|accessdate=17 December 2021}}</ref> and the 2015 [[CRM-Fields-PIMS Prize]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.fields.utoronto.ca/honours/crm-fields-pims_prize.html|title=Fields Institute – CRM-Fields-PIMS Prize Nominations|website=www.fields.utoronto.ca|accessdate=17 December 2021}}</ref> He was elected to the 2018 class of [[fellow]]s of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref name="American Mathematical Society 2018">{{cite web | title=Fellows of the American Mathematical Society | website=[[American Mathematical Society]] | date=26 November 2018 | url=https://www.ams.org/cgi-bin/fellows/fellows_by_year.cgi | access-date=17 December 2021}}</ref> He was also an invited speaker at the ICM 2014<ref>{{Cite web |title=ICM Plenary & Invited Speakers {{!}} International Congress of Mathematicians |url=https://www.mathunion.org/icm-plenary-and-invited-speakers?combine=Behrend |access-date=1 May 2026 |website=www.mathunion.org}}</ref>.
